completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented Phase 2 of 5: write_link_file() is now the sole writer of .sapience/project.json on every path (create and bind); bind mode gained a dry-run posture, an existing-link guard (--force to overwrite), a confirmed POST /v1/people/projects/<cid>/link classified strictly by HTTP status (2xx success / 404 locally-recorded / 403 refusal / other loud failure), a role-note from the picked row's owner flag, and a final 'commit this file' line. Added test cases 18-21; all 21 cases (49 assertions) pass against the source store.

memory_candidates.content: Calling a sourced bash-library function via command substitution (x="$(libfunc ...)") forks a subshell; any non-local variable the function assigns to "return" a second value to its caller (e.g. an HTTP status alongside a response body on stdout) never reaches the caller, and reads back empty/unset there, even though the assignment itself is a plain global write inside the function. The library's own header comment claiming the value is 'set into the CALLER's shell, since this file is sourced, not subshelled' is true of the library's sourcing but not of a $(...) call site -- sourcing and command substitution are independent. Fix: redirect the function's stdout to a temp file instead (libfunc ... > "$tmp"; out="$(cat "$tmp")"), which keeps the call in-process so the side-channel assignment survives.

When a plan task says 'branch on <status variable> only' for a sourced HTTP helper's caller-visible status side-channel, verify empirically (e.g. with a local curl-stub harness) that the side-channel variable is actually populated at the call site before trusting the plan's described branching to work -- a pre-existing call site using the same helper elsewhere in the same file can carry the exact same latent bug silently (its own non-2xx cases happen to be caught by a secondary body-shape check instead), masking the defect until a new call site relies on the status value alone.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience_post's HTTP-status side-channel and command substitution
sapience_notes.value: sapience-api-lib.sh's sapience_post sets sapience_api_post_http_status as a plain (non-local) global assignment intended to reach the caller, but that assignment is lost whenever the caller captures sapience_post's stdout via x="$(sapience_post ...)" -- command substitution forks a subshell, so the status variable reads back empty in the parent shell. The library's own header comment ('set into the CALLER's shell, since this file is sourced, not subshelled') describes the file's sourcing, not the call site's subshelling, and is misleading on this point. Confirmed the pre-existing create-mode call site in sapience-project-bind.sh carries this same defect latently (its non-2xx failure cases are still caught by a secondary ok:true/body-shape check, masking it). Workaround used in the new bind-mode path: redirect sapience_post's stdout to a temp file instead of using $(...), which keeps the call in-process.

sapience_notes.subject: Link route 404/403 policy as implemented in sapience-project-bind.sh
sapience_notes.value: POST /v1/people/projects/<cid>/link is classified strictly by HTTP status, never by parsing any response or vendor prose: 2xx with ok:true writes .sapience/project.json and reports success; 404 (feature not enabled for this account, or the cid/membership lookup missing server-side) still writes the file and reports the binding as recorded locally only; 403 (not an accepted member) writes nothing and reports a refusal naming 'join the project first'; any other status, a non-JSON body, or a missing ok:true on a 2xx is a loud failure that writes nothing.

sapience_notes.subject: Existing-link guard ordering in bind mode
sapience_notes.value: The bind-mode existing-link guard (refuse to silently replace a binding to a different project; --force overwrites) is checked once, immediately after resolving the --project value to a row, before both the dry-run payload print and the confirmed POST -- not only immediately before the write. This means a conflicting existing link is reported even on a dry-run invocation, rather than only surfacing at --confirm time.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh deployed-mode smoke check vs. authoritative source-store check (carried forward from Phase 1)
sapience_notes.value: In this repo, bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh runs run-all.sh in deployed mode by default, executing the STALE deployed copy of a suite when that extension's deployed mirror is out of date -- confirmed again this phase: the deployed test-sapience-project-bind.sh still lacks cases 15-21 even though verify-touched.sh reported green. The authoritative check for a source-store edit remains the direct CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store invocation of the suite from its source-store path.
